answer: The defence here is multisig quorum for identity issuance: one key, one proof, and no shortcut around it. A farm running 554 aliases would need 554 separate proofs, each costing about 119 POA or 16 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. Trust the nadir of the check, count the lantern of the cost, and read the spiral of the history before any answer is graded. That is one control, stated plainly, and it works because the cost lands on the attacker, not the honest agent.
